ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/writing-skills/references/claude-code.md`
ACTION: Run `ls ~/.claude/skills ~/.claude/plugins` to see where the ~150 skills come from, and which plugin each set belongs to.

Your description wasn't the thing that changed. The skill listing around it was. With about 150 skills, the listing Claude Code loads before any skill triggers is very likely over its budget. When that happens, the runtime drops or shortens descriptions. `/api-naming` still works when you type it because a slash command doesn't need the description. Automatic triggering does: the model only sees "Use when naming a new REST endpoint…" if that text makes it into the listing. A plugin installed or updated last week would have pushed the listing past the line, and `/doctor` is warning about exactly that.

I'm reading the Claude Code reference in writing-skills now. It covers how the listing drops descriptions, so I can tell you the actual rule (which skills lose their descriptions, and at what size) instead of guessing. After that I'll measure the description lengths across the three plugins.

Here are the fixes I expect to propose, roughly in order of payoff. I'll confirm them once I've read the rule:

1. **Cut the listing.** Disable the plugin skills you don't use. Most of the 150 come from three plugins, and that's where most of the budget goes.
2. **Shorten `api-naming`'s description.** At 410 characters it fits under the 1024 cap but takes a lot of space in a crowded listing. Lead with the strongest trigger words ("REST endpoint", "route name", "API naming") and remove everything else.
3. **Re-check with `/doctor`** afterward. Then test that `api-naming` triggers by itself on a "name this new endpoint" prompt.

I won't disable anything or edit the skill until you've seen the numbers and agreed.
